text: It hides in burrows on the reef and punches prey so fast that the water around its fists boils. Its eyes see colors no other creature can.
It darts over ponds on four shimmering wings, snatching gnats from the air. Its ancestors were said to be as large as hawks.
It sleeps for days at a time on the same branch. When it finally moves, it is so slow that moss grows on its fur.
On foggy nights, it bobs above the marsh like a lost lantern. Those who follow its light wander in circles until dawn.
This pangolin curls into a ball of razor-edged scales. Its scales are so prized that poachers once hunted it to the brink.
It stores static electricity in its fluffy cheeks. When startled, it releases a jolt strong enough to stop a heart.
It was carved from a single block of stone to guard a forgotten temple. It has not blinked in a thousand years.
It inflates its spiky body when threatened. A single prick from one of its spines carries enough toxin to fell a grown man.
Mothers once sang to it so their children would sleep. Now it sings back, and anyone who hears the lullaby does not wake for a week.
This anglerfish dangles a glowing lure in the black depths. Prey that swims toward the light is swallowed whole.
It hangs upside down in caves by day. At dusk, thousands pour out at once, and their shrieks can shatter glass.
A wind-up toy that kept marching after its key was lost. It still ticks softly, counting down to something no one remembers.
It spends its whole life inside a hollow tree, sealing the entrance with mud until only its beak shows. Its mate feeds it through the slit.
It lives on the hottest volcano slopes and bathes in lava to keep its stony hide from cracking. When it cools, it turns to obsidian.
It follows the tides across the beach, raising one oversized claw to wave at the sea. Rivals fight by waving harder.
This jellyfish never truly dies. When it grows old, it shrinks back into a child and begins its life again.
It weaves webs between the stars. Sailors who navigate by the night sky sometimes find their constellations rearranged by morning.
A teapot that brewed tea for a hundred years until a spirit settled in it. It pours scalding tea on anyone who forgets to say thank you.
It digs tunnels under farms and pops up to steal turnips. Farmers say you can hear it giggling underground.
It glides from tree to tree on a cape of skin, crackling with static. Its fur stands on end before a thunderstorm.
